correctness.rationale: For unequal loads the same-box product vanishes, giving the ordered-pair coefficient m(m-1) and the subtraction m²p_rp_s. The diagonal B is auxiliary only. On the feasible support the consecutive ratio is ((n-r-s)/(n-s))((m-1)/(m-2)), strictly decreasing for r>0 and constant above one for r=0. The zero forbidden tail preserves unimodality. An independent exact rational recalculation gave Q at s=6,7,11,12 respectively 14348907/17039360, 4782969/4259840, 4782969/3727360, 4782969/7454720 for (m,n,r)=(3,15,3), giving the stated two genuine reversals after deletion of s=3. For central r_n the consecutive ratio crosses one at n-(m-1)r_n, which is strictly inside the support for large n and gives standardized maximizing-load displacement x/rho, up to o(1), including an adjacent-integer tie. Thus the compact central local limit is used at the actual maximizer, not extrapolated to the tails. The Gaussian joint-to-marginal ratio completes to a_m exp(x²/2) times a Gaussian factor centered at x/rho. Here a_m<1 by the displayed polynomial inequality. Below the threshold the entire row is negative eventually; above it the maximum is positive and loads at suitable fixed displacements on each side give negatives. The maximizing loads are then distinct from r_n since x/rho!=x. No sign is claimed at equality.
residual_risks: Finite replay covers the sharpness witness, not the entire bundled sweep. The asymptotic result fixes m, and the true variance diagonal and the critical equality case are excluded.

value.rationale: The sign of dependence between exact occupancy frequencies is not settled by knowing that the loads of two specific boxes are negatively correlated. The result gives a complete finite restriction on where positive covariance can occur, proves that two reversals really occur, and identifies the exact centered-load threshold separating no positive pairs from positive pairs across the entire row. The global maximizer is essential to that distinction.
residual_risks: The critical boundary, simultaneous many-box limits, and the variance diagonal are outside this classification.
